target_customer: Licensed cannabis cultivators, manufacturers and distributors
problem: Cannabis operators must comply with state seed to sale tracking rules such as Metrc while managing inventory, sales and operations with weak tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for cannabis ERP and compliance
product_category: cannabis ERP and seed to sale software

founders.name: Stacey Hronowski
founders.background_notes: YC page and Canix blog (2022-06). Both founders featured in Forbes 30 Under 30 per the blog.

founders.name: Artem Pasyechnyk
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CTO in the Canix Series A post; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Flourish Software
competitors.what: Cannabis seed to sale software integrated with Metrc and BioTrack

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard SaaS with hard integration work: bi-directional Metrc sync, inventory and labor costing across state rules.

defensibility.rationale: Compliance integrations and operational data create switching costs, though other vendors had the same state integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed Canix; in January 2026 Canix acquired competitor Trym.

market_need_then: State mandated tracking requirements and fast growth of licensed operators created demand for compliance software in 2019.

identity.logo: Logo created in 2020, replaced by a new logo announced in March 2023 to be more consistent and recognizable
identity.voice_and_tone: Compliance first, support trained in Metrc

branding.community_and_virality: Won TechCrunch Disrupt 2020 per the YC page and company posts; CB Insights lists TechCrunch Startup Battlefield 200; no merch or fan evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage and a startup contest win, but no sourced evidence that the brand drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Canix built Metrc compliant seed to sale software for cannabis operators, won TechCrunch Disrupt in 2020, raised a $10M Series A in June 2022 and reports about 1,000 facilities across 30 states. It acquired competitor Trym in January 2026, which suggests the vendor field consolidated around the survivors. The company is active and growing, and the advantage appears to be compliance depth and a repeatable sales motion.
notes: The Series A post does not name investors; the three names come from CB Insights and an Emles Venture Partners page seen in search results. Earlier rounds conflict: Seedtable shows a $2.5M seed in February 2020 led by Phyto Partners (also a pre-seed in August 2019), ZoomInfo dates a $2.5M seed to 2021, and an interview reports $1.5M total before the A; none recorded as rounds. Totals vary ($10M, $12.85M, $14M). The Trym acquisition was reported in January 2026 by several outlets, terms undisclosed. Founder education and prior employers not found.
